body.statement: For every \(\kappa\ge2\), the endogenous graph of \(\mathcal O_{\kappa}\) is one directed causal tree, namely a chain. For each selector \(S_i\), the history deleting \(T_i\to S_i\) and the history deleting \(F_i\to S_i\) both satisfy local actual-row hitting and give the same singleton feasible nonactual endogenous-value set \(\{1\}\). Deleting \(T_i\to C_i\) is also locally safe and admits value \(1\) at the later gate \(C_i\) in both histories. It is nevertheless full-graph legal after deleting \(T_i\to S_i\) and illegal after deleting \(F_i\to S_i\), because the latter history retains the directed path \(T_i\to S_i\to\cdots\to C_i\). Thus a direct transfer that keeps only \(G[V]\) and the unaugmented layer state of families of subsets of the endogenous path-variable domains from the causal-tree recurrence of EiterLukasiewicz2006Tractable cannot audit Beckers deletion legality on this parameterized family.
body.justification: The scalable selector family isolates exactly which full-graph reachability information an endogenous-value state omits.
body.gap: The earlier UAI version of EiterLukasiewicz2006Tractable, Section 4.1 and Theorems 4.2--4.3, proves its Halpern--Pearl causal-tree result by recursively propagating families of subsets of each endogenous path-variable domain. This proposition leaves that theorem untouched and shows only that a direct \(G[V]\)-only transfer of that state type cannot certify Beckers edge-deletion legality.
body.consumer: A parameterized regression batch over \(\mathcal O_{\kappa}\) detects backends that collapse two selector histories with identical endogenous value states but different full-graph legality.
